notes_for_prompt_writer: Delay finalizing a segment when you encounter subordinating conjunctions or relative pronouns: German subordinate clauses are typically verb‑final and will overturn a premature split. Abbreviations with dots (e.g. 'Inc.') and day numbers with a dot (e.g. '20.') should not be treated as sentence/clause end. For coordinating conjunctions ('und', 'aber') only split when both sides contain their own finite verb (i.e. two independent clauses); otherwise keep the noun/phrase together. Hyphenated compounds and sequences of capitalized nouns are single lexical units and should not be split.
